_doc: The pieces the Hurdles loop iterates over, in build order. Status and history are updated by the loop; definitions change only with a LOG.md entry. Field meanings are in hurdles/PROTOCOL.md under 'pieces.json'.

pieces.title: Engine foundation
pieces.goal: The skeleton every other piece plugs into: fixed-timestep loop (60 Hz sim, interpolated render), input layer (keyboard/mouse/gamepad, buffering, rebinding table), scene state machine (title/run/pause/gameover/victory), seeded RNG, voxel model format plus greedy mesher with baked per-vertex AO, the showcase router and the window.__GR debug contract.
must_have: window.__GR contract exactly as specified in PROTOCOL.md 'Game contract'
?showcase=<piece-id> router: unknown ids show a readable error screen, not a blank canvas
voxel models defined as text or arrays in src/, meshed once and cached; one draw call per model
pause freezes the sim completely; time scale hook for slow-motion captures
zero console errors on load and during 60 s of idle
pieces.showcase: ?showcase=foundation: a turntable of a test voxel model, input echo overlay, fps and sim-tick readout
pieces.judge_focus: Not blind-judged. The integrator checks it against must_have: correctness, frame pacing, input latency.

pieces.title: Render look
pieces.goal: The frame itself: low-res render target with nearest upscale, orthographic three-quarter camera with texel-snapped motion, palette in src/render/palette.js, lighting (warm point lights against cool ambient), outline and AO treatment, fog/vignette, and any post (palette quantise, dithering). The screenshot someone sees on the itch page.
must_have: pixels never swim or shimmer when the camera moves (texel snapping)
one palette used everywhere, UI included
1-px outlines that read on both dark and lit surfaces
flickering torch light that actually lights nearby voxels
a still frame of an arena reads as a finished pixel-art game, not a tech demo
pieces.showcase: ?showcase=look: a static lit arena vignette with hero, two enemies, torches, props; slow camera pan to test snapping
pieces.judge_focus: Still frames and a slow pan strip. Which one looks like a finished, beautiful game?
pieces.reference_hint: top-rated pixel-art or voxel action/roguelite on itch.io with a strong visual identity

reference.why: Top-down pixel-art action roguelite/roguelike with the strongest visual identity in the genre: per-biome palettes, a warm dynamic light pool that follows the player through dark rooms, chunky readable silhouettes even in chaotic combat, and hit/particle craft the whole "juicy pixel action" movement is built on. Structurally the closest real analogue to Gauntlet-Runner (fixed/near-top-down camera, arena waves, dash-based survival, environmental hazards).

pieces.title: Hero model and animation
pieces.goal: The hooded runner: voxel model with a readable silhouette, and procedural animation for idle breathing, run cycle, dash, a 3-hit attack combo, hurt, death, and spawn-in. Squash and stretch, secondary motion (cloak, scarf), anticipation and follow-through.
must_have: silhouette readable at 1x internal resolution
scarf or cloak with lagging secondary motion
run cycle with contact and passing poses, footstep dust hook
each attack swing has anticipation, smear and recovery frames
facing changes turn quickly but never pop
pieces.showcase: ?showcase=hero: hero on a plinth cycling every animation with its name labelled; keys 1-9 pick an animation
pieces.judge_focus: Frame strips of idle, run, dash, attack combo, hurt, death. Which character feels more alive and appealing?
pieces.reference_hint: top-rated itch.io pixel-art action game with an expressive small player character

reference.why: Top-rated, itch-native, HTML5-playable pixel-art action roguelite with a small, consistently expressive hero (idle, run, shoot, hurt, death all read cleanly at tiny on-screen size), exactly the "expressive small player character" bar this piece needs to clear.

pieces.title: Movement and camera
pieces.goal: How moving feels: acceleration and friction curves, 8-way movement with smooth facing, dash with i-frames, cooldown and after-images, wall collision that slides and never snags, and a camera that leads the movement with a dead-zone, eases, and takes shake from the shared channel.
must_have: start and stop within 2-4 frames: snappy, never floaty, never instant
dash is buffered, has i-frames, and cancels attack recovery
sliding along walls and corners never sticks
camera look-ahead toward movement and aim, texel snapped
pieces.showcase: ?showcase=movement: an obstacle-course room with pillars, corners and narrow gaps, plus a ghost trail showing the last 2 s of positions
pieces.judge_focus: Bursts of starts, stops, turns and dashes around corners. Which movement looks tighter and more responsive?
pieces.reference_hint: top-rated itch.io top-down action game praised for tight movement or dash

reference.why: Top-down pixel-art action-adventure built specifically around a dash (quick dash plus a charged teleport-dash), browser-playable, the strongest available match for starts, stops, turns and dashes around corners.

pieces.title: Combat feel
pieces.goal: Hitting and being hit: 3-hit melee combo with hitboxes that match the swing, hitstop scaled to impact, enemy flash and knockback, damage numbers hook, player hurt with i-frames and red flash, health and death rules, and a crit or finisher on hit 3.
must_have: hitstop, white flash, knockback, spark and sound on every hit, all scaled by damage
combo timing window forgiving but not mashy; the third hit feels heavier
getting hurt is unmistakable but not disorienting
no whiffs where the visual clearly connected
pieces.showcase: ?showcase=combat: hero vs 3 training dummies that show hit counts and knockback, plus one dummy that attacks back slowly
pieces.judge_focus: Bursts through a full combo landing on a target. Which hits feel heavier and more satisfying?
pieces.reference_hint: top-rated itch.io action game praised for juicy combat or hit feel

reference.why: A browser-playable (PICO-8/HTML5) beat-'em-up whose entire premise is landing satisfying punch combos on a stream of enemies, the closest itch.io match to combat's judge_focus (bursts through a full combo landing on a target).

pieces.title: VFX and juice
pieces.goal: A shared pooled particle and effect system in the voxel pixel style (cube particles, pixel sprites), and the effects library: hit-sparks, slash smears, dust puffs, dash after-images, death bursts, spawn portals, embers, light flashes, shockwave rings, pickup sparkles. Other pieces call it; they never make their own particles.
must_have: pooled, no allocation per frame, 2000 particles at 60 fps in the showcase
every effect uses the palette and snaps to the pixel grid
effects have shape and timing (a fast pop then a slow fade), not a uniform spray
ambient embers and dust motes available as a scene layer
pieces.showcase: ?showcase=vfx: an effects reel that plays each effect in turn, labelled, looping; keys cycle effects
pieces.judge_focus: Frame strips of hit-spark, death burst, dash, spawn. Which effects look more crafted and punchy?
pieces.reference_hint: top-rated itch.io pixel-art game known for particle effects and juice

reference.why: Top-rated, browser-playable pixel-art action roguelite whose hit, kill and enemy-entry effects are few, bold, two-tone and precisely timed. That is the "crafted and punchy" bar for hit-spark and death-burst strips, and live 30 fps frames can be captured from it.

pieces.title: Enemies
pieces.goal: Four archetypes with distinct silhouettes and colour: Husk (shambling chaser), Ember Wisp (ranged, kites, fires slow orbs), Brute (telegraphed charge, stuns itself on walls), Mite swarm (tiny, fast, groups of 5). Each has spawn-in, idle, move, clear telegraph, attack, hurt, death, and simple readable AI with separation.
must_have: every attack has a telegraph readable before it hits (pose, flash or ground marker)
enemies never stack into one blob; separation and flanking
deaths are satisfying: burst, flop or shatter, never just vanish
difficulty knobs (hp, speed, aggression) are data, not code
pieces.showcase: ?showcase=enemies: a lineup of all four archetypes with names, then ?showcase=enemies&fight=<type> spawns one against the hero
pieces.judge_focus: Stills of the lineup plus strips of each telegraph and death. Which cast is more readable and characterful?
pieces.reference_hint: top-rated itch.io roguelite or top-down action game with a varied enemy roster

reference.why: Top-rated, browser-playable pixel-art action roguelite (#7 in itch's top-rated HTML5 roguelites) whose horde enemies are the genre's benchmark for reading instantly at a tiny size: dark bodies, glowing eyes, one bold hit flash and a splat. It is the only top-rated action roguelite on itch that can be played live here, so its enemies can be captured in real motion.

pieces.title: Arenas and environment
pieces.goal: Seeded arena generation from hand-authored templates with variation: floor and wall voxel tiles, props (pillars, braziers, bones, rubble, banners), torches, doors that seal and open with ceremony, wave spawning with escalation, and a clear room-clear moment.
must_have: rooms look hand-made, not random: composition, focal props, floor variation
doors slam shut on entry with shake and dust; the clear moment is celebrated
wave composition escalates across the 5 arenas and is seed-reproducible
props break or react when hit where it makes sense
pieces.showcase: ?showcase=arenas&seed=N: fly-through of 5 generated arenas, then one played with waves
pieces.judge_focus: Stills of several rooms and a door-slam strip. Which levels look more handcrafted and inviting?
pieces.reference_hint: top-rated itch.io dungeon crawler or roguelite with handsome room art

reference.why: Top-rated, browser-playable pixel-art dungeon-crawler roguelite whose stone-and-torch crypt rooms and overgrown biome rooms are the closest handcrafted-room match to this piece's judge_focus; it is the same pin the enemies critic already vetted and rejected only for motion-capture reasons that do not block a still-room comparison.

pieces.title: Gauntlet corridors
pieces.goal: The signature segments: short corridors chased by the collapse (a wall of falling rock and embers that advances and kills on contact), with traps (spike floors, swinging blades, fire jets, crumbling tiles) laid out in readable rhythms that reward dashing.
must_have: the collapse is spectacular: falling voxels, dust, rumbling shake, ember glow
every trap telegraphs its timing and is fair on first sight
tension ramps: the collapse speeds up if you dawdle and eases if you are far ahead
reaching the end has a release beat: door slams behind you, the rumble stops
pieces.showcase: ?showcase=gauntlet&seed=N: one corridor played start to finish, with trap timing overlay toggled by T
pieces.judge_focus: Strips of the chase and trap dodges. Which sequence looks more tense and exciting?
pieces.reference_hint: top-rated itch.io game with a chase or escape sequence, or trap-gauntlet platforming

reference.why: The signature mechanic of Pizza Tower is an "escape" sequence: a level-ending sprint away from a screen-filling pursuing threat through the same corridors you just explored, with fleeing enemies and speed-blur used to sell danger and momentum. The closest well-known, top-rated itch.io analogue to "chased by the collapse" gauntlet corridors. Windows-only (not browser-playable), so critiques use the developer's own GIFs/screenshots from the itch page rather than live capture.

pieces.title: Boons and pickups
pieces.goal: About 16 boons with visible effects (for example chain sparks on hit, dash leaves an ember trail, third hit fires a wave, lifesteal motes), rarity tiers, a pick-1-of-3 shrine with beautiful cards, stacking rules, plus currency (soul shards) and heart pickups that are satisfying to collect.
must_have: every boon changes something you can SEE in combat, not just a number
the choice screen is a moment: cards animate in, hover and select feel tactile
pickups vacuum toward the player with a sound ladder
synergies exist between at least 4 pairs of boons
pieces.showcase: ?showcase=boons: the choice screen with 3 random boons; ?showcase=boons&give=<id> puts the hero in a dummy room with that boon
pieces.judge_focus: Stills of the choice screen and strips of boons in action. Which upgrade system looks more exciting?
pieces.reference_hint: top-rated itch.io roguelite with an upgrade or card choice screen

reference.why: The strongest fitting HTML5, browser-playable, top-rated roguelite whose core loop is exactly this piece's job: kill things, hit a pick-1-of-N upgrade screen, watch the upgrades visibly change how you fight. It originated as a free itch.io HTML5 game (still playable there), so it can be captured live rather than from a trailer.

pieces.title: Boss: The Warden
pieces.goal: A big voxel jailer-knight fought in a round arena: intro sequence with name card, 3 phases (sweeping chain, ground slams with shockwaves, summoning husks and caging the arena), each with learnable telegraphs, phase transitions with spectacle, a stagger or punish window, and a triumphant death sequence.
must_have: the intro makes you nervous: camera, name card, roar, arena lights up
every attack is learnable and dodgeable on reaction with a dash
phase transitions are events, not just a stat change
the death sequence is the best-looking moment in the game
pieces.showcase: ?showcase=boss&phase=1|2|3: boss fight starting at that phase; ?showcase=boss&intro=1 plays the intro
pieces.judge_focus: Intro stills and strips of each phase's signature attack. Which boss looks more epic and fair?
pieces.reference_hint: top-rated itch.io pixel-art boss fight or boss-rush game

reference.why: Top-down pixel-art dungeon-crawler roguelite with multiple telegraphed boss fights and an on-screen boss health bar, browser-playable, the strongest itch.io match found for a fixed-camera pixel/voxel boss encounter at 4.5+/50+ ratings (the boss-rush/boss-battle tag intersections with pixel art all topped out well under 50 ratings). Its HTML5 web build is a broken test port per the dev, so critiques use the developer's own official screenshots and promo GIF instead of live capture.

pieces.title: HUD and in-game UI
pieces.goal: In-run UI in the pixel style: hearts or health with a damage drain, dash pips, shard counter that ticks up, boon icon row with tooltips, room progress track (arena/corridor/boss), boss health bar, damage numbers, low-health vignette. Minimal, framed, animated.
must_have: pixel-perfect: integer-scaled, palette-bound, pixel font
every number and bar animates its changes (drain, tick, pulse)
never covers the action; readable at a glance mid-fight
low health is felt (heartbeat pulse and vignette) without being noisy
pieces.showcase: ?showcase=hud: a dummy fight that exercises every HUD element, with keys to take damage, gain shards, add boons
pieces.judge_focus: Mid-fight stills and a damage-taken strip. Which HUD looks more polished and readable?
pieces.reference_hint: top-rated itch.io pixel-art action roguelite with a clean HUD

reference.why: Top-down pixel-art action game with a pristine, minimal action UI showing cooldowns and resources; the strongest browser-playable itch.io reference with a clean HUD that can be judged on polish and visual clarity.

pieces.title: Audio
pieces.goal: Everything synthesised in WebAudio: a jsfxr-style SFX bank (swings, hits by weight, dash, footsteps per surface, enemy barks, pickups ladder, doors, collapse rumble, boss) with per-play pitch variation, plus music: a title theme, an arena combat loop that layers up with intensity, a corridor chase layer, and a boss theme. A mixer with ducking and settings volumes.
must_have: no sound repeats identically twice in a row (pitch or volume variation)
music reacts to game state (combat intensity, chase, low health)
mix is balanced: hits cut through, music never masks telegraph cues
audio starts cleanly after the first user gesture; no clicks or pops
pieces.showcase: ?showcase=audio: a sound board listing every SFX and music stem with keys to play them, plus a waveform or meter
pieces.judge_focus: Critic records audio via the page (MediaRecorder on the master bus) and describes it; judge compares spectrogram strips plus written descriptions. Which soundscape is more satisfying and coherent?
pieces.reference_hint: top-rated itch.io game praised for its soundtrack or sound design, ideally chiptune or synth

pieces.title: Title screen and menus
pieces.goal: The first frame: an animated voxel title scene (the runner at the Gauntlet's mouth, embers, torchlight), a crafted logo, and menus (Start, Settings, Controls, Credits) plus pause. Settings cover volumes, screen shake, flashes and key display. Everything navigable by keyboard, mouse and gamepad, with hover and select juice and sound.
must_have: the first frame after load is already beautiful; no flash of unstyled content
the logo is designed, not just a font
menu navigation has sound, motion and a clear focus state
settings persist in localStorage and apply live
pieces.judge_focus: The first frame, a menu-navigation strip and the settings screen. Which title screen makes you want to press Start?
pieces.reference_hint: top-rated itch.io pixel-art game with a memorable title screen

pieces.title: Run flow and endings
pieces.goal: Stitches a run together: intro drop-in, arena/corridor/boss sequencing with transitions, death sequence (slow-mo, collapse of the screen), a game-over run summary (time, kills, boons taken, cause of death), a victory sequence, instant restart (one key, under 1 s to control), and light meta (best time, unlocked lore line).
must_have: death to back in control takes under 3 s if the player wants
transitions between segments are seamless and styled (wipes, camera moves)
the run summary is a satisfying screen worth screenshotting
a full run is completable, and the seed is shown so runs can be shared
pieces.showcase: ?showcase=run-flow&at=death|victory|summary jumps to each ending; normal play covers the rest
pieces.judge_focus: Strips of the death sequence, summary and victory. Which run loop feels more complete and replayable?
pieces.reference_hint: top-rated itch.io roguelite with a strong death/restart loop
